content.content:
1	# PRD – Product Detail Page (PDP)
2	
3	*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Product, Catalogue and PDP" (PRD), "Cart & Inventory" (CAI), "Payments" (PAY), "Returns and Refunds" (RRC), "Customers, Account, CRM Sync" (CRM), "Order Management" (OM). Last updated: 2026-06-19.*
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Page Structure
8	
9	- Breadcrumb navigation displayed on all PDP pages (PRD-001, confirmed)
10	- Style code (SKU) displayed on PDP (PRD-007, confirmed)
11	- Key supporting information in expandable accordions: **Details, Size & Fit, Care, Shipping & Free Returns** (region-specific content) (PRD-008, confirmed)
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 2. Product Data
16	
17	- Product name, price, sizes, and colour swatches sourced from the **Product API** (fed from AP21, but AP21 may not be the sole source in future — do not hard-code AP21 as the only data provider). Colour swatch assets do not live in AP21 — only colour names (PRD-002, confirmed — requirement updated for clarity 05.05)
18	- Style code (SKU) from product data (PRD-007, confirmed)
19	- "Also available in" / "Only available in" colour swatches; selecting a colour updates the page content and URL (PRD-004, confirmed). Hover-to-preview swatch behaviour (colour updates on rollover without click) is a **custom build, not OOTB, and not scoped for go-live** — see Open Items (PRD-004)
20	- *Open: product copy ownership (description, editorial text) — Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 is TBD (see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies")*
21	
22	---
23	
24	## 3. Product Badges & Tags (PRD-005 – PRD-006, confirmed)
25	
26	- Products can carry one or more badges: **Campaign, Runway, Exclusive, Online Exclusive, VIC Exclusive** — badge *assignment* on applicable products is confirmed (PRD-005)
27	- Multiple badges per product are supported; a defined display priority/hierarchy applies when more than one badge is present
28	- Badge creation must not require a code deployment (PRD-005, comment: "ideally the creation of these badges would not require a code change")
29	- **Badges are clickable** and navigate the customer to a PLP view filtered to products in that badge category (PRD-005, confirmed — workbook updated 2026-06-19: "captured in requirement"). See also plp.md §2.6.
30	- *Design caveat: badges not yet present in PLP designs ("Missing badges in PLP") (PRD-005)*
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 4. Product States (PRD-010 – PRD-017, confirmed)
35	
36	- **Coming Soon** — product is displayed on PDP before stock is added or purchase is enabled
37	- **Back in Soon** — product has sold out but will restock imminently (re-cut)
38	- **Unavailable (size-level)** — triggers the Notify Me flow for the affected size variant
39	- OOS sizes visually greyed out/disabled; Add to Bag is suppressed for that size variant (PRD-014)
40	- All product states (Coming Soon, Back in Soon, Unavailable) must comply with **Google Merchant Centre** feed rules — ineligible-state products must not surface in product feeds (PRD-017)
41	- Low-stock indicator at size level: displays **"LOW"** label — purely visual, does not alter CTA behaviour or block add-to-bag (PRD-012; also PRD-030 from CAI)
42	
43	---
44	
45	## 5. Pricing Display
46	
47	- Display price in storefront currency (AUD, USD, GBP, EUR)
48	- Sale pricing: was/now format (PRD-003, confirmed — subject to designs). If price changes again after being put on sale, only "now" updates; "was" is retained (REG-042, confirmed)
49	- Tax label per storefront: GST (AU), VAT (UK/EU), Tax (US) (PAY, confirmed)
50	- **Duties and taxes information** displayed country-specifically on PDP (PRD-013, confirmed)
51	- **DDP/DDU messaging** displayed on PDP per applicable countries (PAY-059, confirmed)
52	- Max configurable purchase quantity enforced per customer group (PRD-011, confirmed)
53	- *Open: HK/ME/US Intl/EU Intl pricing display — Global-e pricing via SFCC price books is defined and REG-041 is confirmed (REG-040 retired). Sign-off of the full mechanism (PRC-34..PRC-43) is still pending; do not implement until confirmed.*
54	
55	---
56	
57	## 6. Availability & Add to Bag
58	
59	*Buffer stock rules apply on PDP. See [cart.md](cart.md) section 5 for the full buffer stock system.*
60	
61	- Per-size availability shown (ADD TO BAG / OUT OF STOCK / low-stock "LOW" indicator)
62	- **ADD TO BAG** shown when quantity is above buffer threshold
63	- **OUT OF STOCK** shown when quantity is at or below buffer threshold (back-in-stock capture presented)
64	- Low-stock indicator at size level — no quantity number shown — displays "LOW" label
65	- **Max 3 units per SKU** (same size + colour) enforced at add-to-cart (CAI-017, confirmed)
66	- **No soft reservation** at add-to-cart (CAI-032, confirmed)
67	
68	---
69	
70	## 7. Primary CTAs & Supporting Links (PRD-018 – PRD-022, confirmed)
71	
72	- **Add to Bag** — primary CTA when in stock
73	- **Find in Boutique** — opens as a **slide-out** (not a modal) alongside Add to Bag (PRD-018)
74	- **Wishlist icon** — displayed alongside the primary CTA; size must be selected before wishlist save (PRD-019, PRD-020)
75	- Supporting links: **Unavailable** (opens slide-out notify me form), **Find My Size**, **Size Guide** (PRD-021)
76	- **Need Assistance** section: links to email, live chat (with availability hours caveat), and Contact Us (PRD-022). The "Contact Us" link is an external redirect to the Zendesk-hosted contact form — there is no embedded Zendesk integration in the storefront.
77	
78	---
79	
80	## 8. Find in Boutique (CAI-037 – CAI-042, PRD-028 – PRD-039)
81	
82	The "Find in Boutique" CTA is shown on all eligible products. The feature opens as a **flyout/slide-out panel** (not a modal). All Find in Boutique requirements are now **confirmed** but carry a **Phase 2** design caveat (design not yet available — "Phase 2").
83	
84	### Panel contents
85	- "Find in Boutique" CTA only displays for products where in-store stock checking is supported (PRD-028, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
86	- At top of panel: product thumbnail, product name, selected colour, and price (PRD-029, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
87	- **Size selector** pre-populated from the PDP selection; customer can change size within the panel (PRD-030, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
88	- A **real-time inventory call** to NewStore via MuleSoft is made once a size is selected; the call refreshes when the customer selects a different size (CAI-038)
89	- **No auto-refresh** while the panel is open; boutique stock cached with configurable TTL (CAI-042)
90	- **Location search field** to filter boutique results (PRD-031, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
91	- **"Use My Location"** option triggers browser geolocation with explicit permission; handles failure case gracefully with inline message (PRD-032, PRD-033, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
92	- **Maps integration** via Google Maps (via MRT API connection) for boutique directions (PRD-034, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
93	- Per-boutique results show: name, address, distance (if geolocation permitted), stock status (**In Stock / Low Stock – Contact Boutique to Confirm Availability / Out of Stock**), opening hours, contact details, current live open status (e.g. "OPEN – CLOSES AT 6:00PM"), map pin, and a view more button (PRD-035, confirmed). Opening hours and live open status are sourced from the **Google Business API** (with a manual override available in Business Manager) — distinct from the Google Maps integration used for the map pin and directions (TPI: Google Business API; Google Maps).
94	- **Get Directions** link per boutique result, opening the location in a maps application (PRD-036, confirmed)
95	- Configurable limit on number of boutique results displayed (PRD-039, confirmed)
96	- Display a clear message when no boutiques carry the selected size (CAI-041)
97	- **No buffer stock** applied to boutique inventory (CAI-040)
98	- Fully responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile (PRD-037, confirmed)
99	- Enter key triggers search in the location field (PRD-038, confirmed)
100	
101	---
102	
103	## 9. Back-in-Stock Notifications / Stock Alert (OM-033 – OM-034, PRD-040 – PRD-049, confirmed)
104	
105	Shown when product/size is OOS (Unavailable state):
106	
107	- Stock alert CTA/link displayed on PDP when selected size is OOS (PRD-040)
108	- Opens as a slide-out with the stock alert sign-up form: product name, price, and product image thumbnail at top (PRD-041, PRD-042)
109	- **Multiple size selection supported** — customer selects which unavailable sizes to register for (PRD-043)
110	- Customer name and email captured as required fields; **pre-populated and editable for authenticated customers** (PRD-044)
111	- **Marketing opt-in/out checkbox** compliant with regional consent requirements, gated by Omneo consent management (PRD-045)
112	- Clear submission CTA to register the stock alert (PRD-046)
113	- Confirmation message shown within the slide-out on successful submission (PRD-047)

# PRD – Product Detail Page (PDP)

*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Product, Catalogue and PDP" (PRD), "Cart & Inventory" (CAI), "Payments" (PAY), "Returns and Refunds" (RRC), "Customers, Account, CRM Sync" (CRM), "Order Management" (OM). Last updated: 2026-06-19.*

---

## 1. Page Structure

- Breadcrumb navigation displayed on all PDP pages (PRD-001, confirmed)
- Style code (SKU) displayed on PDP (PRD-007, confirmed)
- Key supporting information in expandable accordions: **Details, Size & Fit, Care, Shipping & Free Returns** (region-specific content) (PRD-008, confirmed)

---

## 2. Product Data

- Product name, price, sizes, and colour swatches sourced from the **Product API** (fed from AP21, but AP21 may not be the sole source in future — do not hard-code AP21 as the only data provider). Colour swatch assets do not live in AP21 — only colour names (PRD-002, confirmed — requirement updated for clarity 05.05)
- Style code (SKU) from product data (PRD-007, confirmed)
- "Also available in" / "Only available in" colour swatches; selecting a colour updates the page content and URL (PRD-004, confirmed). Hover-to-preview swatch behaviour (colour updates on rollover without click) is a **custom build, not OOTB, and not scoped for go-live** — see Open Items (PRD-004)
- *Open: product copy ownership (description, editorial text) — Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 is TBD (see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies")*

---

## 3. Product Badges & Tags (PRD-005 – PRD-006, confirmed)

- Products can carry one or more badges: **Campaign, Runway, Exclusive, Online Exclusive, VIC Exclusive** — badge *assignment* on applicable products is confirmed (PRD-005)
- Multiple badges per product are supported; a defined display priority/hierarchy applies when more than one badge is present
- Badge creation must not require a code deployment (PRD-005, comment: "ideally the creation of these badges would not require a code change")
- **Badges are clickable** and navigate the customer to a PLP view filtered to products in that badge category (PRD-005, confirmed — workbook updated 2026-06-19: "captured in requirement"). See also plp.md §2.6.
- *Design caveat: badges not yet present in PLP designs ("Missing badges in PLP") (PRD-005)*

---

## 4. Product States (PRD-010 – PRD-017, confirmed)

- **Coming Soon** — product is displayed on PDP before stock is added or purchase is enabled
- **Back in Soon** — product has sold out but will restock imminently (re-cut)
- **Unavailable (size-level)** — triggers the Notify Me flow for the affected size variant
- OOS sizes visually greyed out/disabled; Add to Bag is suppressed for that size variant (PRD-014)
- All product states (Coming Soon, Back in Soon, Unavailable) must comply with **Google Merchant Centre** feed rules — ineligible-state products must not surface in product feeds (PRD-017)
- Low-stock indicator at size level: displays **"LOW"** label — purely visual, does not alter CTA behaviour or block add-to-bag (PRD-012; also PRD-030 from CAI)

---

## 5. Pricing Display

- Display price in storefront currency (AUD, USD, GBP, EUR)
- Sale pricing: was/now format (PRD-003, confirmed — subject to designs). If price changes again after being put on sale, only "now" updates; "was" is retained (REG-042, confirmed)
- Tax label per storefront: GST (AU), VAT (UK/EU), Tax (US) (PAY, confirmed)
- **Duties and taxes information** displayed country-specifically on PDP (PRD-013, confirmed)
- **DDP/DDU messaging** displayed on PDP per applicable countries (PAY-059, confirmed)
- Max configurable purchase quantity enforced per customer group (PRD-011, confirmed)
- *Open: HK/ME/US Intl/EU Intl pricing display — Global-e pricing via SFCC price books is defined and REG-041 is confirmed (REG-040 retired). Sign-off of the full mechanism (PRC-34..PRC-43) is still pending; do not implement until confirmed.*

---

## 6. Availability & Add to Bag

*Buffer stock rules apply on PDP. See [cart.md](cart.md) section 5 for the full buffer stock system.*

- Per-size availability shown (ADD TO BAG / OUT OF STOCK / low-stock "LOW" indicator)
- **ADD TO BAG** shown when quantity is above buffer threshold
- **OUT OF STOCK** shown when quantity is at or below buffer threshold (back-in-stock capture presented)
- Low-stock indicator at size level — no quantity number shown — displays "LOW" label
- **Max 3 units per SKU** (same size + colour) enforced at add-to-cart (CAI-017, confirmed)
- **No soft reservation** at add-to-cart (CAI-032, confirmed)

---

## 7. Primary CTAs & Supporting Links (PRD-018 – PRD-022, confirmed)

- **Add to Bag** — primary CTA when in stock
- **Find in Boutique** — opens as a **slide-out** (not a modal) alongside Add to Bag (PRD-018)

- Supporting links: **Unavailable** (opens slide-out notify me form), **Find My Size**, **Size Guide** (PRD-021)
- **Need Assistance** section: links to email, live chat (with availability hours caveat), and Contact Us (PRD-022). The "Contact Us" link is an external redirect to the Zendesk-hosted contact form — there is no embedded Zendesk integration in the storefront.

---

## 8. Find in Boutique (CAI-037 – CAI-042, PRD-028 – PRD-039)

The "Find in Boutique" CTA is shown on all eligible products. The feature opens as a **flyout/slide-out panel** (not a modal). All Find in Boutique requirements are now **confirmed** but carry a **Phase 2** design caveat (design not yet available — "Phase 2").

- "Find in Boutique" CTA only displays for products where in-store stock checking is supported (PRD-028, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- At top of panel: product thumbnail, product name, selected colour, and price (PRD-029, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- **Size selector** pre-populated from the PDP selection; customer can change size within the panel (PRD-030, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- A **real-time inventory call** to NewStore via MuleSoft is made once a size is selected; the call refreshes when the customer selects a different size (CAI-038)
- **No auto-refresh** while the panel is open; boutique stock cached with configurable TTL (CAI-042)

- Per-boutique results show: name, address, distance (if geolocation permitted), stock status (**In Stock / Low Stock – Contact Boutique to Confirm Availability / Out of Stock**), opening hours, contact details, current live open status (e.g. "OPEN – CLOSES AT 6:00PM"), map pin, and a view more button (PRD-035, confirmed). Opening hours and live open status are sourced from the **Google Business API** (with a manual override available in Business Manager) — distinct from the Google Maps integration used for the map pin and directions (TPI: Google Business API; Google Maps).
- **Get Directions** link per boutique result, opening the location in a maps application (PRD-036, confirmed)
- Configurable limit on number of boutique results displayed (PRD-039, confirmed)
- Display a clear message when no boutiques carry the selected size (CAI-041)
- **No buffer stock** applied to boutique inventory (CAI-040)
- Fully responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile (PRD-037, confirmed)
- Enter key triggers search in the location field (PRD-038, confirmed)

- Stock alert CTA/link displayed on PDP when selected size is OOS (PRD-040)

- Whether the "Find My Size" link is shown/suppressed based on Measmerize data availability is managed by the Measmerize widget, not SFCC (PRD-052 removed as not applicable for SFCC)

- Size conversion tables appropriate to the selected product type (PRD-054)

1	# Zimmermann - Salesforce PWA Kit (Production)
2	
3	> **STRICT RULE — TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.**
4	> Every file created or modified under `overrides/` **must** use `.ts` or `.tsx`.
5	> `.js` and `.jsx` files are not acceptable here, including theme files, stories, and config modules.
6	> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`.
7	
8	Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com, a luxury Australian fashion brand. Must be robust and secure and SEO-friendly. See [.docs/architecture.md](.docs/architecture.md) for stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths.
9	
10	Tier classifications and protected-file lists live in [.claude/rules/](.claude/rules/) — loaded automatically per session. Custom slash commands for scaffolding and review live in [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/).
11	
12	## Branch Rules
13	
14	**At session start, always run `git branch --show-current`.** If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — do not make any changes.
15	
16	| Branch                    | Branched from          | Merges to                                                                       | Allowed?      | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
17	| ------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
18	| `feature/*`               | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       | ✅ Yes        | Primary working context for new work                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
19	| `fix/*`                   | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       | ✅ Yes        | Non-urgent bug fixes. Mechanically identical to `feature/*` — naming is for commit hygiene                                                                                                                                                                                |
20	| `release/*`               | `develop`              | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        | ⚠️ Supervised | Plan-first + confirm-every-edit required. Code logic fixes must use a `fix/release-*` sub-branch                                                                                                                                                                          |
21	| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch, then forward-merged to `develop` once the release ships | ✅ Yes        | Only path for code logic fixes on a release. PR targets the release branch; SIT gate runs against the PR. Treated like `feature/*` on the sub-branch itself — the "Supervised" plan-first + confirm-every-edit rules apply only to direct edits on the `release/*` branch |
22	| `hotfix/*`                | `main`                 | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        | ✅ Yes        | Urgent production fixes only. Tier 1 rules still apply. Must be back-merged to `develop` to prevent drift                                                                                                                                                                 |
23	| `develop`                 | —                      | —                                                                               | ❌ Never      | Human commits only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
24	| `main`                    | —                      | —                                                                               | ❌ Never      | Human commits only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
25	
26	> **On `release/*` or `hotfix/*` branches you MUST read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) before any action.** It holds the supervised-edit rules (plan-first, confirm-every-edit, `fix/release-*` sub-branch flow) and the GitFlow back-merge rules that apply in addition to the Hard Rules below. On `feature/*` and `fix/*`, ignore it.
27	
28	## Hard Rules
29	
30	1. **Never operate on `develop` or `main`** branches.

95	| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

108	## Commands
109	
110	- `npm start` — local dev at http://localhost:3000. **Do not run!** Ask the user to restart if needed.
111	- `npm run build`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run push` (Managed Runtime deploy)

113	## Accessibility
114	
115	Target WCAG 2.2 AA. Fall back to 2.1 AA only where 2.2 is technically infeasible — document why.

117	## Rules
118	
119	*Day-to-day code-writing conventions live in `.claude/rules/` and load automatically:
120	[conventions.md](.claude/rules/conventions.md) (cross-cutting: naming, imports, DRY, security),
121	[typescript.md](.claude/rules/typescript.md) (TS idioms), [css.md](.claude/rules/css.md)
122	(Chakra tokens, `.scss`), and [components.md](.claude/rules/components.md)
123	(component/hook/utility structure, Storybook categorisation, composition). The rules below
124	are project-specific behaviours and security guardrails that don't fit there.*
125	
126	- **No mocking:** All data must come from the live Commerce Cloud API via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hooks. No MSW or hardcoded fixtures in production paths.

128	- **Comments:** Do not remove existing commented-out code or comments (except when removing the corresponding code) — leave for the user to delete manually. (For _new_ comments introduced in a PR, see conventions.md.)
129	- **Icons:** Use `overrides/app/components/icons` — this is the single source of truth for all icons (Zimmermann custom and base PWA). 135

139	_Per-storefront Didomi defaults, GTM/Enhanced Conversions setup, and Inside Chat rules: see [.docs/prd/regional.md](.docs/prd/regional.md)._

141	## Type Definitions
142	
143	- **Component-specific prop types:** co-locate at the top of the component file.

145	- Don't re-declare types already exported by `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` or `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` — import them directly.
146	
147	## Testing
148	
149	Three layers: **Vitest** (unit logic) · **Storybook** `play` (component interactions) · **Playwright** (E2E). Write tests only where failure would be non-obvious or costly to debug — data mapping, integration boundaries, complex state, and pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken. Every UI component needs a `.stories.tsx`; every logic-heavy feature needs a `.test.ts` or a story `play`.
150	
151	Full layer guidance, file layout, selector priority, and mocking policy: [.claude/rules/testing.md](.claude/rules/testing.md). (The no-MSW rule in Rules applies to production paths only.)
152	
153	## Graceful Degradation
154	
155	Each external system must fail independently — one outage must not break the whole page. Two defaults override any per-system behaviour: **fail closed on consent** (if consent state is unknown, load no third-party scripts), and **never silently substitute a different checkout, payment, or commerce flow** when an integration is down — surface an explicit error instead.
156	
157	## Performance
158	
159	Mobile page speed is a top priority. Every change that touches rendering, data fetching, or assets must not regress it.
160	
161	- **LCP budget is tight (≤ 2s at p75 mobile)** — Defer every third-party script that isn't required for first paint. Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM, Optimizely, Inside Chat, Narvar EDD, reCAPTCHA, etc.) must not block LCP — use `defer`, `async`, or post-hydration injection. If a new third-party integration looks like it might land on the critical path, flag it before merging.
162	- **Images:** Always use lazy loading and serve correctly sized images. Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
163	- **Code splitting:** Prefer dynamic `import()` for heavy components not needed on initial render.
164	- **Data fetching:** Avoid over-fetching — request only the fields you need. Waterfall requests are not acceptable; parallelise where possible.
165	- **Bundle size:** Do not introduce large dependencies without confirming with the user.
166	- **Dependencies:** Before implementing any feature that may require a third-party library, check `package.json` for what is already installed. Evaluate whether an existing dependency can satisfy the requirement. If a better third-party option exists, present the recommendation (existing vs. new, with trade-offs) and wait for user approval before installing anything.
167	
168	## Gotchas
169	
170	- **Theme runtime errors:** Custom components (e.g. `ListMenu`) must be defined in the theme object or destructuring will throw.
171	- **Commerce SDK types not importable:** Check `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/dist/` for generated definitions, or declare a narrow local `type`.
172	- **Magento password migration:** Passwords were not migrated from Magento — all existing customers must reset at go-live. Do not assume any saved credentials exist. Account creation and login flows must handle this gracefully (CFD-013).
173	
174	## Requirements
175	
176	Requirements for this project are in `.docs/`, they must be strictly followed.
177	Before any code changes, verify logic against relevant `.docs/` files.
178	For any task that touches an external integration, check the matching `.docs/integration/NN-*.md` doc.
179	
180	If a requirement is missing, ambiguous, or not yet confirmed — **stop, flag the ambiguity, propose a solution, and wait for user approval before proceeding.** Do not fill gaps with assumptions.
181	
182	Verification: Start every task by briefly stating which doc/section you are following (e.g. "Implementing per auth.md section 2.1" or "Implementing per 07-adyen.md §3").
183	
184	**Doc integrity:** Confirmed PRDs (`.docs/prd/`) and finalised Figma designs are the source of truth for _requirements_. `.docs/integration/` docs are guides for _how_ each integration works technically. If a user instruction contradicts either, pause immediately — cite the specific doc, section, and requirement ID — and ask the user whether the doc should be updated or the instruction is a deliberate override. Do not proceed silently either way. The same applies if you spot any improvement or conflict within the docs themselves.
185	
186	## Living Memory
187	
188	`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Read [.docs/memory/projectState.md](.docs/memory/projectState.md) at the start of every session (or run `/session-start`). For what belongs in each memory file and when to update it, see the [session-start skill](.claude/skills/session-start/SKILL.md).
189	
190	**Open items that block implementation** are listed under "Unresolved Dependencies" in [.docs/memory/projectState.md](.docs/memory/projectState.md). Ask the user before hard-coding assumptions about any of them.
191	
192	---
193	
194	_Human-developer onboarding now lives on Confluence: [Claude Code CLI — Developer Onboarding Guide](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/304775192) (session checklist, prompting guide), [1.2 Team Overview](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/261586947) (contacts), and [Claude Code Skills Reference](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/297959425) (useful skills) — not loaded into Claude's context._
195	
196	---
197	
198	_This file is Tier 1 — changes require both squad leads and the Integration lead._

# Zimmermann - Salesforce PWA Kit (Production)

> **STRICT RULE — TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.**

> `.js` and `.jsx` files are not acceptable here, including theme files, stories, and config modules.
> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`.

Tier classifications and protected-file lists live in [.claude/rules/](.claude/rules/) — loaded automatically per session. Custom slash commands for scaffolding and review live in [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/).

## Branch Rules

**At session start, always run `git branch --show-current`.** If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — do not make any changes.

| Branch                    | Branched from          | Merges to                                                                       | Allowed?      | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `feature/*`               | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       | ✅ Yes        | Primary working context for new work                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `fix/*`                   | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       | ✅ Yes        | Non-urgent bug fixes. Mechanically identical to `feature/*` — naming is for commit hygiene                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `release/*`               | `develop`              | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        | ⚠️ Supervised | Plan-first + confirm-every-edit required. Code logic fixes must use a `fix/release-*` sub-branch                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch, then forward-merged to `develop` once the release ships | ✅ Yes        | Only path for code logic fixes on a release. PR targets the release branch; SIT gate runs against the PR. Treated like `feature/*` on the sub-branch itself — the "Supervised" plan-first + confirm-every-edit rules apply only to direct edits on the `release/*` branch |
| `hotfix/*`                | `main`                 | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        | ✅ Yes        | Urgent production fixes only. Tier 1 rules still apply. Must be back-merged to `develop` to prevent drift                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `develop`                 | —                      | —                                                                               | ❌ Never      | Human commits only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `main`                    | —                      | —                                                                               | ❌ Never      | Human commits only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

> **On `release/*` or `hotfix/*` branches you MUST read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) before any action.** It holds the supervised-edit rules (plan-first, confirm-every-edit, `fix/release-*` sub-branch flow) and the GitFlow back-merge rules that apply in addition to the Hard Rules below. On `feature/*` and `fix/*`, ignore it.

13. **Never use `--dangerously-skip-permissions`** on `release/**`, `main`, or `develop`. This flag bypasses all edit confirmations and is only permitted in CI automation contexts, never in interactive developer sessions on shared or protected branches.

If a task depends on a component, hook, or integration that belongs to a later sprint, stop and ask whether to build a placeholder or whether that sprint is already complete.

The SFCC sites are hard routing and config boundaries — **never bleed config across sites.** Never assume a storefront's routing, URL prefix, checkout ownership, or consent defaults without checking [.docs/prd/regional.md](.docs/prd/regional.md).

## Commands

- `npm start` — local dev at http://localhost:3000. **Do not run!** Ask the user to restart if needed.
- `npm run build`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run push` (Managed Runtime deploy)

## Accessibility

Target WCAG 2.2 AA. Fall back to 2.1 AA only where 2.2 is technically infeasible — document why.

## Rules

*Day-to-day code-writing conventions live in `.claude/rules/` and load automatically:
[conventions.md](.claude/rules/conventions.md) (cross-cutting: naming, imports, DRY, security),
[typescript.md](.claude/rules/typescript.md) (TS idioms), [css.md](.claude/rules/css.md)
(Chakra tokens, `.scss`), and [components.md](.claude/rules/components.md)
(component/hook/utility structure, Storybook categorisation, composition). The rules below
are project-specific behaviours and security guardrails that don't fit there.*

- **No mocking:** All data must come from the live Commerce Cloud API via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hooks. No MSW or hardcoded fixtures in production paths.
- **Environment variables:** Never hardcode secrets, tokens, API keys, or credentials anywhere in the codebase. All such values must be defined in `.env` (local dev, gitignored) and set as platform environment variables on Managed Runtime for staging/prod. When adding a new env var: (1) add it to `.env` with the real value, (2) add it to `.env.sample` (with the value only if it is a non-secret public identifier, otherwise leave the value blank). Never put tokens, bearer credentials, DSNs, or licence keys in `.env.sample`.
- **Comments:** Do not remove existing commented-out code or comments (except when removing the corresponding code) — leave for the user to delete manually. (For _new_ comments introduced in a PR, see conventions.md.)
- **Icons:** Use `overrides/app/components/icons` — this is the single source of truth for all icons (Zimmermann custom and base PWA). Do not import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons` directly. If a required icon is missing from the overrides set, ask the user — do not substitute a visually different one.
- **Styling:** Chakra UI component props first; use a `.scss` file alongside the component only when Chakra props are insufficient. The `overrides/app/theme/` folder is the source of truth — brand tokens in `foundation/` (Tier 1), one file per component override in `components/` (Tier 2), composed in `index.ts`. Register a new component override in `theme/components/index.ts`.
- **Minimal changes:** Make the smallest change that fully achieves the task. Do not remove or replace existing base template functionality unless explicitly instructed. When a larger change (e.g., a refactor for cleanliness) seems beneficial, propose it and wait for user confirmation — never do it silently.
- **Copy-first rule:** For any task that requires overriding base template files that do not yet exist in `overrides/`, the very first step is to prepare all of them at once: (1) copy each file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`, (2) convert each to TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`) and update relevant imports, (3) run `npx tsc --noEmit`, (4) add a temporary `console.log` to each copied file identifying it (e.g. `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')`) so the user can verify the override is rendering instead of the base component, then **stop and present the converted files to the user to test**. Wait for the user to confirm the overrides are rendering before making any functional changes; remove the `console.log` statements once confirmed. Never skip this step or bundle it silently with functional changes.

## Consent & Marketing

- **Didomi:** Do not load any third-party script until Didomi consent is granted. Gate all analytics, marketing, and tracking scripts behind Didomi callbacks.
- **Marketing opt-in:** Unchecked by default on all storefronts except US (pre-checked). Sync opt-in state: FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys.

_Per-storefront Didomi defaults, GTM/Enhanced Conversions setup, and Inside Chat rules: see [.docs/prd/regional.md](.docs/prd/regional.md)._

## Type Definitions

- **Component-specific prop types:** co-locate at the top of the component file.
- **Shared types** (Commerce Cloud entities, API responses, shared hook signatures): `overrides/app/types/` — split into `commerce.ts`, `components.ts`, `hooks.ts`, re-exported via `index.ts`.
- Don't re-declare types already exported by `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` or `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` — import them directly.

## Testing

Three layers: **Vitest** (unit logic) · **Storybook** `play` (component interactions) · **Playwright** (E2E). Write tests only where failure would be non-obvious or costly to debug — data mapping, integration boundaries, complex state, and pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken. Every UI component needs a `.stories.tsx`; every logic-heavy feature needs a `.test.ts` or a story `play`.

Full layer guidance, file layout, selector priority, and mocking policy: [.claude/rules/testing.md](.claude/rules/testing.md). (The no-MSW rule in Rules applies to production paths only.)

## Graceful Degradation

Each external system must fail independently — one outage must not break the whole page. Two defaults override any per-system behaviour: **fail closed on consent** (if consent state is unknown, load no third-party scripts), and **never silently substitute a different checkout, payment, or commerce flow** when an integration is down — surface an explicit error instead.

## Performance

Mobile page speed is a top priority. Every change that touches rendering, data fetching, or assets must not regress it.

- **LCP budget is tight (≤ 2s at p75 mobile)** — Defer every third-party script that isn't required for first paint. Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM, Optimizely, Inside Chat, Narvar EDD, reCAPTCHA, etc.) must not block LCP — use `defer`, `async`, or post-hydration injection. If a new third-party integration looks like it might land on the critical path, flag it before merging.
- **Images:** Always use lazy loading and serve correctly sized images. Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
- **Code splitting:** Prefer dynamic `import()` for heavy components not needed on initial render.
- **Data fetching:** Avoid over-fetching — request only the fields you need. Waterfall requests are not acceptable; parallelise where possible.
- **Bundle size:** Do not introduce large dependencies without confirming with the user.
- **Dependencies:** Before implementing any feature that may require a third-party library, check `package.json` for what is already installed. Evaluate whether an existing dependency can satisfy the requirement. If a better third-party option exists, present the recommendation (existing vs. new, with trade-offs) and wait for user approval before installing anything.

## Gotchas

- **Theme runtime errors:** Custom components (e.g. `ListMenu`) must be defined in the theme object or destructuring will throw.
- **Commerce SDK types not importable:** Check `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/dist/` for generated definitions, or declare a narrow local `type`.
- **Magento password migration:** Passwords were not migrated from Magento — all existing customers must reset at go-live. Do not assume any saved credentials exist. Account creation and login flows must handle this gracefully (CFD-013).

## Requirements

Requirements for this project are in `.docs/`, they must be strictly followed.
Before any code changes, verify logic against relevant `.docs/` files.
For any task that touches an external integration, check the matching `.docs/integration/NN-*.md` doc.

If a requirement is missing, ambiguous, or not yet confirmed — **stop, flag the ambiguity, propose a solution, and wait for user approval before proceeding.** Do not fill gaps with assumptions.

Verification: Start every task by briefly stating which doc/section you are following (e.g. "Implementing per auth.md section 2.1" or "Implementing per 07-adyen.md §3").

**Doc integrity:** Confirmed PRDs (`.docs/prd/`) and finalised Figma designs are the source of truth for _requirements_. `.docs/integration/` docs are guides for _how_ each integration works technically. If a user instruction contradicts either, pause immediately — cite the specific doc, section, and requirement ID — and ask the user whether the doc should be updated or the instruction is a deliberate override. Do not proceed silently either way. The same applies if you spot any improvement or conflict within the docs themselves.

## Living Memory

`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Read [.docs/memory/projectState.md](.docs/memory/projectState.md) at the start of every session (or run `/session-start`). For what belongs in each memory file and when to update it, see the [session-start skill](.claude/skills/session-start/SKILL.md).

**Open items that block implementation** are listed under "Unresolved Dependencies" in [.docs/memory/projectState.md](.docs/memory/projectState.md). Ask the user before hard-coding assumptions about any of them.

---

---

1	# PRD – Data Migration, SEO, GEO & URL
2	
3	*Last updated: 2026-06-11*
4	
5	Scope: Magento→SFCC data migration, URL strategy and redirects, SEO (canonicals/hreflang, sitemaps/robots, rendering/headings/meta, structured data), and GEO routing foundations. Regional storefront routing, consent, and currency live in [regional.md](regional.md).
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Data Migration (DMU-001 – DMU-012)
10	
11	- Product feed via MuleSoft from AP21 to SFCC covering ~1,600 active SKUs: names, descriptions, attributes, imagery refs, category assignments (DMU-001). Ongoing product sync via MuleSoft post-migration. **DMU-002 — Confirmed (status flipped from Ready for Sign Off, 2026-06-11).** The PWA-side contract is settled: SFCC displays exactly what MuleSoft returns for product data (JT 04-06), with AP21 as the master of record. Upstream sourcing (the first load draws from **both AP21 and PLM** via MuleSoft, with Magento-enriched data migrated after the initial load) sits **outside the PWA boundary** — the PWA does not enrich or compute product attributes itself, it renders the MuleSoft payload. The earlier RJ challenges (PLM/Magento enrichment) are upstream-of-MuleSoft concerns, not PWA blockers.
12	- Multi-region catalogue assignments and regional merchandising preserved across all storefronts (DMU-003).
13	- Registered customer records (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-25): **only email address and Omneo ID** are migrated to SFCC. Name, phone number, saved delivery addresses, and communication preferences are sourced **live from Omneo at login**, not held in SFCC. The previously requested 20-address cap is no longer relevant (addresses are not stored in SFCC). FE must treat Omneo as the source of customer profile data post-login; degrade gracefully if Omneo is unreachable.
14	- **Customer passwords are not migrated** — customers must reset on first login (DMU-005). See AGENTS.md "Magento password migration" gotcha.
15	- Saved payment card details are **not** migrated; customers re-enter at next purchase (DMU-006).
16	- Historical order records are **not** migrated into SFCC. Order history is accessed via NewStore **through MuleSoft** where customer identifiers match across online and in-store channels (DMU-007, **Confirmed 2026-06-11** — status flipped from Ready for Sign Off). The PWA displays exactly what MuleSoft returns for customer order history (JT 04-06); no order data is held in SFCC. ⚠️ Source-of-truth flag retained: the requirement text + JT name **NewStore via MuleSoft**, while an RJ comment says **"Order history will come from Omneo"** — the upstream source (NewStore vs Omneo behind MuleSoft) is out of the PWA boundary but remains unreconciled; see Open Items. For the ME storefront, only online orders appear in My Account order history; the orders API returns the most recent 50 orders held in NewStore, and until NewStore transitions in ME only online orders are visible — no FE customisation required to filter retail orders (DMU-008, Ready for Sign Off 2026-05-25).
17	- Contentful API connections reconfigured to point at the new platform; no bulk content re-entry needed (DMU-009, **challenged → Open** — RJ: no longer required as AS will be setting up Contentful; reconciliation pending). Mechanism note: Contentful integrates as the headless CMS via the **Salesforce App Exchange connector**, consuming content through the Contentful **delivery API** for all customer-facing pages across all storefronts (Third Party Integrations: CMS / Contentful) — i.e. the integration is the App Exchange connector, not a bespoke API rewire.
18	- Product images and digital assets (DMU-010, de-scoped 2026-05-25): **out of scope for migration.** Images and assets are stored and served from Contentful — there is no CDN migration, no asset URL rewrite, and no 301 redirects for asset URLs. The existing Contentful API connection is simply reconfigured to point at the new SFCC platform as part of go-live (covered by DMU-009). (Source note records the **new** platform CDN as **Akamai** (SFCC default), whereas the **current** setup is **Cloudflare** (DMU-020). These are not in conflict — they describe current vs new platform CDN — but the migration must carry existing Cloudflare redirect/SEO rules forward to Akamai; see §2 DMU-019/DMU-020. No asset-migration impact, as assets stay in Contentful.)
19	- Migration approach: initial bulk export + one or more timestamp-based delta migrations + a final delta close to DNS cutover (DMU-011). Migration scripts must be repeatable and capable of multiple delta runs — one-off scripts are not acceptable (DMU-012).
20	- **Wishlist migration (Confirmed):** customer wishlist data migrated from Magento, wishlist items mapped to corresponding SFCC product records and associated to the migrated account via Omneo ID. FE renders the migrated wishlist post-login.
21	- **Product enrichment migration (Confirmed):** badges, category assignments, colour swatches, colour grouping, swatch images, and Shop the Look associations migrated from Magento to SFCC, mapped to the corresponding product/catalogue structure (Shop the Look display logic TBD).
22	- **Notify Me migration (Confirmed):** active Notify Me (back-in-stock) subscriptions migrated from Magento — customer email addresses and product IDs carried forward and mapped to SFCC product records.
23	
24	---
25	
26	## 2. URL Strategy (DMU-013 – DMU-020)
27	
28	- Existing storefront locale prefix conventions preserved (DMU-013) — see [regional.md](regional.md) Section 1.
29	- AU configured as root with no locale prefix and designated x-default hreflang target (DMU-016, **Resolved** — AU root stays globally crawlable; the bot allowlist in REG-009 exempts search engines and social unfurlers from the human geo-redirect, so `x-default` continues to point at the AU root).
30	- Existing product URL `.html` suffix preserved to maintain indexed URLs and avoid unnecessary 301 overhead (DMU-015).
31	- Category URLs updated for SEO consolidation (e.g. `/clothing/dresses`); 301s applied from all legacy category paths (DMU-014).
32	- 301 permanent redirects implemented for all URLs that change as a result of migration — products, categories, content, assets (DMU-017).
33	- All redirects implemented per the redirect mapping document, produced during build phase and validated pre go-live (DMU-018, **Open** — Accenture to propose redirect ownership; Zimmermann IT to review existing CDN rules).
34	- All 301s managed at CDN/edge level to minimise application-layer impact (DMU-019, **Open** — existing CDN redirect and SEO rules must be identified and carried forward, not auto-transferred).
35	- Existing CDN redirect rules and SEO configuration from the current Cloudflare setup preserved and carried forward to the new platform CDN (DMU-020).
36	
37	---
38	
39	## 3. SEO (DMU-021 – DMU-041)
40	
41	### Canonicals & hreflang
42	- Canonical tags output on all indexable pages, referencing the preferred URL for the storefront (DMU-021).
43	- Filtered and faceted PLP URLs canonicalise to the unfiltered base PLP URL to prevent duplicate-content indexation (DMU-022, **Open** — Zimmermann wants the ability to override the canonical on selected indexable filter pages).
44	- hreflang tags applied only on canonical PDP URLs; non-canonical PDP variants do not carry hreflang but **do** retain canonical tags (DMU-023).
45	- hreflang implemented via XML sitemap format, mapping all locale codes to their respective storefront URLs (DMU-024).
46	- hreflang tags consolidated from the current 200+ country-specific tags to ~12 regional/language-level tags (DMU-025) — final structure to be confirmed with the Sparro SEO team prior to implementation.
47	
48	### Sitemaps & robots
49	- XML sitemaps auto-generated per storefront and locale, refreshed daily (DMU-026). Disabled and deleted pages excluded on regeneration (DMU-027). Homepage URLs include trailing slash (DMU-028). URLs blocked in `robots.txt` must not appear in any sitemap (DMU-029).
50	- `robots.txt` permits crawling of indexable pages including the bag page; restricts checkout flow, account pages, search results, and filtered URL parameters (DMU-036).
51	
52	### Rendering, headings & meta
53	- All product, category, and content pages rendered **server-side (SSR)** for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS (DMU-030).
54	- Title tags per page in the format `[Product Name] [Colour] | Zimmermann` — the legacy "Online" token has been removed as it consumes character space without value. Configurable via BM meta tag rules (DMU-031, updated 2026-05-15).
55	- Unique meta description tags per product and category page, sourced from product and catalogue data in SFCC. Category page metadata remains editable per page and is not auto-applied across all pages (DMU-032, Ready for Sign Off — Zimmermann to clarify what "auto-applied across pages" means before final sign-off).
56	- Single H1 per page template (homepage, PLP, PDP), correct H2–H6 hierarchy, no duplicate heading tags (DMU-033). PDP H1 includes the product colour (DMU-034).
57	- CMS-editable on-page SEO content field on all category and PLP pages, configurable at individual storefront level (DMU-035, partial resolution 2026-05-15): **SEO rules and attributes will live in SFCC per storefront** (not Contentful). Still Open: Sparro to define field schema before custom build.
58	
59	### Structured data
60	- Product and Merchant Listing Schema on all PDPs per Sparro template (DMU-037) — custom build required, not OOTB in SFCC PWA Kit.
61	- CollectionPage, BreadcrumbList, and ItemList Schema on all PLPs per Sparro template (DMU-038) — custom build, Accenture + Sparro to confirm JSON-LD scope and page types.
62	- LocalBusiness Schema on individual boutique location detail pages per Sparro template (DMU-039) — custom build.
63	- Organisation Schema on each regional storefront homepage per Sparro template, with `url` and `contactPoint` fields configured per storefront (DMU-040) — custom build.
64	- Structured data for products includes available sizes and per-offer availability, driven by real-time inventory data (DMU-041).
65	
66	---
67	
68	## 4. GEO (DMU-042)
69	
70	The system will deliver the technical foundations required for **post-launch GEO (Generative Engine Optimisation) enablement** — SSR, structured data, canonical URLs, and XML sitemaps — ensuring no architectural decisions block future GEO activation (DMU-042). No GEO-specific features are in launch scope.
71	
72	---
73	
74	## 5. Open Items
75	
76	See **AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies"** for the full list. Data migration / URL / SEO / GEO open items:
77	
78	- Redirect mapping ownership and existing CDN/SEO rule audit (DMU-018, DMU-019)
79	- PLP canonical override on indexable filter pages (DMU-022)
80	- Category meta description "auto-applied across pages" — Zimmermann to clarify the concern before sign-off (DMU-032)
81	- CMS-editable on-page SEO field — field schema to be defined by Sparro (DMU-035, location resolved as SFCC)
82	- **Order history upstream source (DMU-007)** — DMU-007 itself is now **Confirmed** for the PWA (display exactly what MuleSoft returns; §1). What remains open is the *upstream* source behind MuleSoft: the requirement + JT (04-06) say **NewStore via MuleSoft**, RJ says **"Order history will come from Omneo"**. This is out of the PWA boundary but should be reconciled so the integration contract is unambiguous.
83	- **Contentful API reconfiguration (DMU-009)** — RJ challenge: "This is no longer required as AS will be setting up Contentful." Reconcile whether DMU-009 still applies.
84	
85	**Resolved since previous version:**
86	- DMU-004 customer migration — updated: email + Omneo ID only; profile sourced live from Omneo
87	- DMU-008 ME order history — handled by NewStore API; no FE customisation
88	- DMU-010 asset CDN migration — de-scoped: assets remain in Contentful
89	- DMU-031 meta title format — "Online" token removed
90	- DMU-016 AU x-default hreflang — resolved by REG-009 bot allowlist; AU root stays crawlable, `x-default` remains AU (the prior "globally accessible URL TBD" open note is now struck in source)
91	- New Confirmed migration scope added — Magento wishlist, product enrichment (badges/swatches/colour grouping/Shop the Look), and Notify Me subscriptions (§1)
92	- DMU-002 product data source of record — **Confirmed 2026-06-11**: PWA displays exactly what MuleSoft returns; AP21 master; PLM/Magento enrichment is upstream of MuleSoft, out of PWA boundary
93	- DMU-007 order history — **Confirmed 2026-06-11**: PWA displays exactly what MuleSoft returns; no SFCC store (upstream NewStore-vs-Omneo source still to reconcile, above)
94

Ongoing product sync via MuleSoft post-migration. **DMU-002 — Confirmed (status flipped from Ready for Sign Off, 2026-06-11).** The PWA-side contract is settled: SFCC displays exactly what MuleSoft returns for product data (JT 04-06), with AP21 as the master of record. Upstream sourcing (the first load draws from **both AP21 and PLM** via MuleSoft, with Magento-enriched data migrated after the initial load) sits **outside the PWA boundary** — the PWA does not enrich or compute product attributes itself, it renders the MuleSoft payload. The earlier RJ challenges (PLM/Magento enrichment) are upstream-of-MuleSoft concerns, not PWA blockers.
- Multi-region catalogue assignments and regional merchandising preserved across all storefronts (DMU-003).
- Registered customer records (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-25): **only email address and Omneo ID** are migrated to SFCC. Name, phone number, saved delivery addresses, and communication preferences are sourced **live from Omneo at login**, not held in SFCC. The previously requested 20-address cap is no longer relevant (addresses are not stored in SFCC). FE must treat Omneo as the source of customer profile data post-login; degrade gracefully if Omneo is unreachable.
- **Customer passwords are not migrated** — customers must reset on first login (DMU-005). See AGENTS.md "Magento password migration" gotcha.
- Saved payment card details are **not** migrated; customers re-enter at next purchase (DMU-006).
- Historical order records are **not** migrated into SFCC. Order history is accessed via NewStore **through MuleSoft** where customer identifiers match across online and in-store channels (DMU-007, **Confirmed 2026-06-11** — status flipped from Ready for Sign Off). The PWA displays exactly what MuleSoft returns for customer order history (JT 04-06); no order data is held in SFCC. ⚠️ Source-of-truth flag retained: the requirement text + JT name **NewStore via MuleSoft**, while an RJ comment says **"Order history will come from Omneo"** — the upstream source (NewStore vs Omneo behind MuleSoft) is out of the PWA boundary but remains unreconciled; see Open Items. For the ME storefront, only online orders appear in My Account order history; the orders API returns the most recent 50 orders held in NewStore, and until NewStore transitions in ME only online orders are visible — no FE customisation required to filter retail orders (DMU-008, Ready for Sign Off 2026-05-25).
- Contentful API connections reconfigured to point at the new platform; no bulk content re-entry needed (DMU-009, **challenged → Open** — RJ: no longer required as AS will be setting up Contentful; reconciliation pending). Mechanism note: Contentful integrates as the headless CMS via the **Salesforce App Exchange connector**, consuming content through the Contentful **delivery API** for all customer-facing pages across all storefronts (Third Party Integrations: CMS / Contentful) — i.e. the integration is the App Exchange connector, not a bespoke API rewire.
- Product images and digital assets (DMU-010, de-scoped 2026-05-25): **out of scope for migration.** Images and assets are stored and served from Contentful — there is no CDN migration, no asset URL rewrite, and no 301 redirects for asset URLs. The existing Contentful API connection is simply reconfigured to point at the new SFCC platform as part of go-live (covered by DMU-009). (Source note records the **new** platform CDN as **Akamai** (SFCC default), whereas the **current** setup is **Cloudflare** (DMU-020). These are not in conflict — they describe current vs new platform CDN — but the migration must carry existing Cloudflare redirect/SEO rules forward to Akamai; see §2 DMU-019/DMU-020. No asset-migration impact, as assets stay in Contentful.)
- Migration approach: initial bulk export + one or more timestamp-based delta migrations + a final delta close to DNS cutover (DMU-011). Migration scripts must be repeatable and capable of multiple delta runs — one-off scripts are not acceptable (DMU-012).
- **Wishlist migration (Confirmed):** customer wishlist data migrated from Magento, wishlist items mapped to corresponding SFCC product records and associated to the migrated account via Omneo ID. FE renders the migrated wishlist post-login.
- **Product enrichment migration (Confirmed):** badges, category assignments, colour swatches, colour grouping, swatch images, and Shop the Look associations migrated from Magento to SFCC, mapped to the corresponding product/catalogue structure (Shop the Look display logic TBD).
- **Notify Me migration (Confirmed):** active Notify Me (back-in-stock) subscriptions migrated from Magento — customer email addresses and product IDs carried forward and mapped to SFCC product records.

---

## 2. URL Strategy (DMU-013 – DMU-020)

- Existing storefront locale prefix conventions preserved (DMU-013) — see [regional.md](regional.md) Section 1.
- AU configured as root with no locale prefix and designated x-default hreflang target (DMU-016, **Resolved** — AU root stays globally crawlable; the bot allowlist in REG-009 exempts search engines and social unfurlers from the human geo-redirect, so `x-default` continues to point at the AU root).
- Existing product URL `.html` suffix preserved to maintain indexed URLs and avoid unnecessary 301 overhead (DMU-015).
- Category URLs updated for SEO consolidation (e.g. `/clothing/dresses`); 301s applied from all legacy category paths (DMU-014).
- 301 permanent redirects implemented for all URLs that change as a result of migration — products, categories, content, assets (DMU-017).
- All redirects implemented per the redirect mapping document, produced during build phase and validated pre go-live (DMU-018, **Open** — Accenture to propose redirect ownership; Zimmermann IT to review existing CDN rules).
- All 301s managed at CDN/edge level to minimise application-layer impact (DMU-019, **Open** — existing CDN redirect and SEO rules must be identified and carried forward, not auto-transferred).
- Existing CDN redirect rules and SEO configuration from the current Cloudflare setup preserved and carried forward to the new platform CDN (DMU-020).

---

## 3. SEO (DMU-021 – DMU-041)

### Canonicals & hreflang
- Canonical tags output on all indexable pages, referencing the preferred URL for the storefront (DMU-021).
- Filtered and faceted PLP URLs canonicalise to the unfiltered base PLP URL to prevent duplicate-content indexation (DMU-022, **Open** — Zimmermann wants the ability to override the canonical on selected indexable filter pages).
- hreflang tags applied only on canonical PDP URLs; non-canonical PDP variants do not carry hreflang but **do** retain canonical tags (DMU-023).
- hreflang implemented via XML sitemap format, mapping all locale codes to their respective storefront URLs (DMU-024).
- hreflang tags consolidated from the current 200+ country-specific tags to ~12 regional/language-level tags (DMU-025) — final structure to be confirmed with the Sparro SEO team prior to implementation.

### Sitemaps & robots
- XML sitemaps auto-generated per storefront and locale, refreshed daily (DMU-026). Disabled and deleted pages excluded on regeneration (DMU-027). Homepage URLs include trailing slash (DMU-028). URLs blocked in `robots.txt` must not appear in any sitemap (DMU-029).
- `robots.txt` permits crawling of indexable pages including the bag page; restricts checkout flow, account pages, search results, and filtered URL parameters (DMU-036).

### Rendering, headings & meta
- All product, category, and content pages rendered **server-side (SSR)** for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS (DMU-030).
- Title tags per page in the format `[Product Name] [Colour] | Zimmermann` — the legacy "Online" token has been removed as it consumes character space without value. Configurable via BM meta tag rules (DMU-031, updated 2026-05-15).
- Unique meta description tags per product and category page, sourced from product and catalogue data in SFCC. Category page metadata remains editable per page and is not auto-applied across all pages (DMU-032, Ready for Sign Off — Zimmermann to clarify what "auto-applied across pages" means before final sign-off).
- Single H1 per page template (homepage, PLP, PDP), correct H2–H6 hierarchy, no duplicate heading tags (DMU-033). PDP H1 includes the product colour (DMU-034).
- CMS-editable on-page SEO content field on all category and PLP pages, configurable at individual storefront level (DMU-035, partial resolution 2026-05-15): **SEO rules and attributes will live in SFCC per storefront** (not Contentful). Still Open: Sparro to define field schema before custom build.

### Structured data
- Product and Merchant Listing Schema on all PDPs per Sparro template (DMU-037) — custom build required, not OOTB in SFCC PWA Kit.
- CollectionPage, BreadcrumbList, and ItemList Schema on all PLPs per Sparro template (DMU-038) — custom build, Accenture + Sparro to confirm JSON-LD scope and page types.
- LocalBusiness Schema on individual boutique location detail pages per Sparro template (DMU-039) — custom build.
- Organisation Schema on each regional storefront homepage per Sparro template, with `url` and `contactPoint` fields configured per storefront (DMU-040) — custom build.
- Structured data for products includes available sizes and per-offer availability, driven by real-time inventory data (DMU-041).

---

## 4. GEO (DMU-042)

The system will deliver the technical foundations required for **post-launch GEO (Generative Engine Optimisation) enablement** — SSR, structured data, canonical URLs, and XML sitemaps — ensuring no architectural decisions block future GEO activation (DMU-042). No GEO-specific features are in launch scope.

---

## 5. Open Items

See **AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies"** for the full list. Data migration / URL / SEO / GEO open items:

- Redirect mapping ownership and existing CDN/SEO rule audit (DMU-018, DMU-019)
- PLP canonical override on indexable filter pages (DMU-022)
- Category meta description "auto-applied across pages" — Zimmermann to clarify the concern before sign-off (DMU-032)
- CMS-editable on-page SEO field — field schema to be defined by Sparro (DMU-035, location resolved as SFCC)
- **Order history upstream source (DMU-007)** — DMU-007 itself is now **Confirmed** for the PWA (display exactly what MuleSoft returns; §1). What remains open is the *upstream* source behind MuleSoft: the requirement + JT (04-06) say **NewStore via MuleSoft**, RJ says **"Order history will come from Omneo"**. This is out of the PWA boundary but should be reconciled so the integration contract is unambiguous.
- **Contentful API reconfiguration (DMU-009)** — RJ challenge: "This is no longer required as AS will be setting up Contentful." Reconcile whether DMU-009 still applies.

**Resolved since previous version:**
- DMU-004 customer migration — updated: email + Omneo ID only; profile sourced live from Omneo
- DMU-008 ME order history — handled by NewStore API; no FE customisation
- DMU-010 asset CDN migration — de-scoped: assets remain in Contentful
- DMU-031 meta title format — "Online" token removed
- DMU-016 AU x-default hreflang — resolved by REG-009 bot allowlist; AU root stays crawlable, `x-default` remains AU (the prior "globally accessible URL TBD" open note is now struck in source)
- New Confirmed migration scope added — Magento wishlist, product enrichment (badges/swatches/colour grouping/Shop the Look), and Notify Me subscriptions (§1)
- DMU-002 product data source of record — **Confirmed 2026-06-11**: PWA displays exactly what MuleSoft returns; AP21 master; PLM/Magento enrichment is upstream of MuleSoft, out of PWA boundary
- DMU-007 order history — **Confirmed 2026-06-11**: PWA displays exactly what MuleSoft returns; no SFCC store (upstream NewStore-vs-Omneo source still to reconcile, above)
